title: Revit connector how-to document
description: One task, the shortest correct path to doing it on a given Revit version, and the mistakes that path avoids. Interchange format for the how-to corpus (see howto-corpus-design.md). One document per JSONL line. Unknown top-level fields are ALLOWED so an older broker can still read a newer corpus (it ignores what it does not know and reports the newer corpus_version in guidance); the fields it does know are validated strictly. Cross-field rules the Go validator enforces beyond this schema: absorbs excludes own id; contributors[].rev <= rev; updated_at >= created_at; hit/miss query shape.

schema_version.description: Schema revision this document was written against. A broker validates the fields it knows and ignores the rest; when the corpus declares a schema_version above the broker's, every response says so in guidance (howto-corpus-newer-than-broker).

id.description: Lineage id: a kebab-case slug chosen when the document is first created and never renamed. Edits keep the id and bump `rev`, so a reference (describe_howto, a local override, a link in another document) stays valid across revisions. Uniqueness is checked against the shared corpus at triage and against local + embedded corpora by submit_howto, which appends -2, -3 … on a clash.

kind.description: howto: a working path to a task (the normal kind). pitfall: a single mistake and its fix, without a full task script, for a mistake that is a task in its own right. negative: reserved for 'the API cannot do this and there is no route' -- when a how-to exists, its task sentence states the missing API and no separate negative document is written.

title.description: Short noun phrase, the way a person would name the example.

task.description: The task in agent language: one or two plain sentences naming the element type, the operation, and the key member nouns of the answer. This is the primary search text, so every word should earn its place; no preamble, no rationale.

queries.description: Recorded phrasings from real sessions. Misses are the most valuable rows: they are where API search failed and this document earns its keep.

hit.description: Phrasings that found the right member or this document.

miss.description: Phrasings that did NOT surface the answer, with what they surfaced instead.

members.description: Fully-qualified Namespace.Type.Member names the script calls (describe_function's 'member' shape; constructors as Type.#ctor, generic arity with a backtick). Indexed for exact-name hits and used to cross-link API results. Empty is legal for kind=negative, whose 'related' member (the one that does NOT exist) goes in pitfalls[].members as free text.

script.description: The complete, runnable C# script body in the connector's current dialect (reads at top level; writes inside Connector.WithTransaction; return a value). Comments in the script ARE the explanation: label setup as setup, number the steps of the recipe, and say why at the step where it matters. There is no separate prose summary. Required for kind=howto. 16 KB bound; aim well under 3 KB.

symptom.description: What the agent sees: the error text, the wrong result, the silent nothing.

members.description: Members this pitfall is about, when different from the document's. Free text (a negative how-to names a member that does not exist).

pitfalls.description: One entry per mistake the path avoids. Indexed text.

tags.description: Facets (walls, views, sheets, worksharing, transactions, groups). Indexed at low weight for search and returned on every hit; also used for browsing and de-duplication.

api_since.description: Declared hint: first Revit version whose API offers the members used. Not verification.

api_until.description: Declared hint: last Revit version before a used member was removed or deprecated.

kind.description: harness/validation-corpus: extracted from a repo test. submission: arrived through submit_howto and the review queue. local: written by submit_howto into the user's own corpus, never reviewed. maintainer: authored directly in the repo.

ref.description: Where it came from: a test function name (harness), an issue URL (submission), a validation-corpus case number.

reviewed_by.description: GitHub login of the reviewer, or 'review-agent', set when accepted into the shared corpus. Never set on a local document.

provenance.description: Maintainer-facing only: never returned by search_howto or describe_howto, and never indexed. Credit lives in `contributors`, which is agent-visible.

rev.description: Revision of this lineage, from 1. The corpus file holds only the latest revision per id (git history keeps the rest); an improvement is the same id with rev+1 replacing the line. rev exists so references and verification stamps can name the revision they meant.

contributors.description: Credit, agent-visible: who authored and improved this lineage, accumulated across revisions (a new revision appends, never rewrites). Opt-in: submit_howto only records a handle the submitter passed as credit_as; nothing is inferred from git, gh or the machine. Returned by describe_howto.

handle.description: A GitHub login or a display name the submitter chose (letters, digits, space, dot, underscore, hyphen). Never an email (no @) or a machine/host name (no backslash or slash).

role.description: author: created rev 1. contributor: submitted a later revision. reviewer: triaged it into the shared corpus (optional; maintainers may decline credit).

rev.description: The revision this credit applies to; must not exceed the document's rev (validator check; triage renumbers on acceptance).

absorbs.description: Lineage MERGE record, set only at triage: ids of other lineages folded into this one. Their lines are deleted from the corpus; describe_howto on an absorbed id follows the pointer here. Must not contain this document's own id.

text.description: The query as sent to search_functions or search_howto.

rank.description: For hits: the rank the answer appeared at.

surfaced.description: For misses: what came back instead, in a few words.

ranker.description: The ranker value the response reported, so a recorded rank is read against the ranker that produced it. Episodes recorded before #107 shipped were served by the add-in's tiered ranker, which is what keyword-fallback names today.

query.description: A recorded phrasing. In queries.hit, rank is required and surfaced absent; in queries.miss, surfaced is required and rank absent (enforced by the validator).
